title: A Robot Walks into a Bar: Can Language Models Serve as Creativity Support Tools for Comedy? An Evaluation of LLMs’ Humour Alignment with Comedians

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation through interactive comedy-writing sessions and focus group discussions with professional comedians, focusing on the models' default to Western norms, shallow adjustments to non-dominant cultures (e.g., retaining Western names in non-Western settings), and cultural homogenization.

Qualitative evaluation via focus groups and writing sessions, observing the models' uneven safety filtering (e.g., refusing a comedic monologue from an Asian woman's perspective while allowing one from a white man) and inability to authentically represent Black comedic voices.
Qualitative evaluation during comedian workshops, highlighting the models' tendency to sanitize outputs by removing 'gay language' and defaulting to heteronormative perspectives.
Qualitative evaluation based on comedians' interactive prompting, noting the models' default to male mainstream perspectives and intersectional disparities in content moderation and generation.
